newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks weaker, summer lull may be short.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks weaker, summer lull may be short.

text.p: Most Croatian stocks lost ground on Tuesday in moderate trade, with stronger investor demand after recent losses helped blue chips Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka up.
Traders said the summer lull could be short-lived.

"There are players who may not leave the market altogether this summer, so a new upward trend might start earlier or the 'dead season' could be shorter," said Josko Milisa of I.C.F. brokerage. "Still, trading volume will shrink."
Only four of 17 active issues rose, seven fell and six were flat. Volume rose to 12,489 from 10,097 units but turnover fell to 7.3 million kuna from 10.1 million last Friday.

Top gainer Pliva pharmaceuticals added 20 kuna or 4.25 percent to 490 kuna on volume of 2,686 shares, making it the second most actively traded stock. Its global depositary receipts (GDRs), representing 1/5 of each share, also rose to $16.125 on the London Stock Exchange.
"There is some talk about Pliva taking over a company abroad and it is also thought to have had good first half results," Milisa said, explaining greater buying interest.
Zagrebacka's ordinaries firmed 13 kuna to 1,963 on volume of 560, following the rise of its 1/10 GDRs to $32.5 from Monday's $32.25 on Seaq.
Varazdinska Banka's first issue was most active with 2,968 shares sold. They closed three kuna higher at 215.
Biggest decliner was electrical group Koncar, losing 80 kuna or 6.78 percent to 1,000 kuna with 69 shares sold.
Brewery Karlovacka Pivovara, a subsidiary of Chile's Compania Cervecerias Unidas CCUY.O, slipped 28 kuna to 560 on volume of 1,054 units.
"This is a correction after too steep a rise. There is nothing wrong with its fundamentals," said Milisa.
He mentioned food processor Podravka as a completely opposite case and more exposed to speculation. Podravka continued to slide, ending at 248 kuna with 2,255 shares sold.
"The market is tired of waiting for its 1996 results or news of managerial changes, this has taken too long. It needs a better first half report to break the downward trend," he added.
Chocolate maker Kras held firm at 425 kuna on volume of 203 after announcing that it would raise 60 million German marks in syndicated funds this summer for modernisation and development.
